{{Short description|none}}
The [[United States|U.S.]] {{nobreak|[[Minnesota|State of Minnesota]]}} currently has 34 [[Statistical area (United States)|statistical areas]] that have been delineated by the [[Office of Management and Budget]] (OMB). On July 21, 2023, the OMB delineated six [[combined statistical area]]s, nine [[metropolitan statistical area]]s, and 19 [[micropolitan statistical area]]s in Minnesota.<ref name=OMB_20230721>{{cite web |subject=Revised Delineations of Metropolitan Statistical Areas, Micropolitan  Statistical Areas, and Combined Statistical Areas, and Guidance on Uses of  the Delineations of These Areas |date=July 21, 2023 |title=0MB BULLETIN NO. 23-01 |url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/OMB-Bulletin-23-01.pdf |access-date=October 23, 2023 |publisher=[[Office of Management and Budget]]}}</ref> As of 2025, the largest of these is the [[Minneapolis-St. Paul-St. Cloud, MN-WI CSA|Minneapolis–St. Paul, MN-WI CSA]], comprising the area around the state's [[twin cities]] — [[Minneapolis]], its largest city, and [[St. Paul, Minnesota|St. Paul]], its capital.

{{clear}}
